prompt.context: Our client, Hamm's University, is a mid-size not-for-profit private university in the Midwest of the United States, well-known for its liquid gold colored sports uniforms. Over the last few years, Hamm's University has received less state and federal aid, leading to a negative net margin. However, other universities near us have overcome this issue and haven't seen margin erosion. The Board of Regents has engaged our firm to help the University strengthen its position.
prompt.question: The Board wants to increase net income by $25M per year within 2 years (net income was -$5M last year). How should Hamm's University achieve this goal?

clarifying_info.a: Near a city with a population of ~450,000 in a state with a population of ~7M. A majority of students are from the same state or surrounding states.
Yes — there are 2 other private universities and a large state school within an hour of Hamm's.

clarifying_info.q: What sports division does Hamm's compete in?

clarifying_info.a: Yes — several graduate schools with programs in Medicine, Law, Dentistry, Business, Psychology, and Engineering.
The Psychology and Economics departments are highly ranked in faculty prowess and research.

exhibits.title: YOY Statement of Activities (2017 & 2018) and KPIs
exhibits.shows: Year-over-year income statement for Hamm's University (2017 vs 2018) broken down by revenue line items and cost line items, plus selected KPIs such as enrollment, faculty researchers, grants awarded, endowment balance, and active alumni donors.

exhibits.title: Schools Comparison (2018 Data)
exhibits.shows: 2018 financial statements and KPIs for three comparable institutions: Public 1 (a large state school), Private 1, and Private 2, with the same revenue and cost line items as Exhibit 1 plus selected KPIs.

framework: Revenue: Analyze all revenue streams — Net Tuition (undergraduate + R&B), Federal & State Aid, Grants & Contracts, Endowment Income, Athletics, Alumni Gifts
Costs: Examine cost structure — Instruction, Research, Operations, Administration, Materials & Supplies
Industry / Competitive Benchmarking: Compare Hamm's financials and KPIs against nearby schools (Public 1, Private 1, Private 2) to identify gaps and replicable strategies
Student Body Composition: Understand enrollment trends and mix of undergrad vs. graduate students
Learn from Peers: Identify which competitors overcame the same aid decline and determine what is feasible to replicate

questions.prompt: Walk through Exhibit 1. What are the key drivers of Hamm's margin deterioration from 2017 to 2018?
questions.guidance: Strong answer identifies: (1) Total revenue dropped $35M (from $580M to $545M) while total costs rose $20M (from $530M to $550M), swinging net income from +$50M to -$5M — a $55M swing. (2) The biggest revenue declines are Federal & State Aid (-$35M), Grants & Contracts (-$50M), and Endowment Income (-$4M). Net Tuition actually increased +$54M. (3) On the cost side, Instruction rose $22M and Administration rose $2M; most other cost lines are relatively flat. The core problem is revenue — especially the collapse in grants and aid.

math.setup: Revenue change: 545 - 580 = -35. Cost change: 550 - 530 = +20. NI swing: -35 - 20 = -55 (from +50 to -5).
steps: Largest revenue declines: Federal/State Aid -$35M (100→65), Grants & Contracts -$50M (80→30), Endowment Income -$4M (15→11)
math.answer: Net income swung -$55M YOY. The primary drivers are a $35M drop in federal/state aid and a $50M drop in grants & contracts, partially offset by a $54M increase in net tuition.

questions.prompt: Now look at Exhibit 2. Which of the nearby schools is most similar to Hamm's and which revenue strategy is most feasible to replicate?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare Hamm's (2018: revenue $545M, 13,800 undergrads, 50 researchers, endowment $195M, 20,000 alumni donors) to the three peers. Private 1 and Private 2 are closest in size/revenue. Key differentiators: Private 1 has a $1.1B endowment and 35,000 active alumni donors — hard to replicate quickly. Private 2 has only $300M endowment but generates $150M in Grants & Contracts with 85 researchers and 145 grants. Hamm's has only $30M in grants with 50 researchers. Private 2's grant-heavy model is more replicable because it relies on hiring researchers and leveraging Hamm's already-prestigious Psychology department — not on a large donor base or massive endowment.

questions.prompt: The board wants to increase NI by $25M/year. Assume: each researcher generates 1.6 grants/year; each grant is worth ~$1M revenue; each researcher costs $400K; administration costs add $50K per researcher. How many additional faculty researchers does Hamm's need to hire?
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up the equation: NI gain per researcher = revenue per researcher - cost per researcher. Revenue per researcher = 1.6 grants × $1M = $1.6M. Cost per researcher = $400K + $50K = $450K. Net margin per researcher = $1.6M - $0.45M = $1.15M. Researchers needed = $25M / $1.15M ≈ 22 researchers.

math.answer: Hamm's needs to hire approximately 22 additional faculty researchers to achieve the $25M NI goal.

brainstorming.prompt: What are other ways Hamm's University could improve its financial position beyond the research/grants strategy?

categories.name: Revenue — Tuition
ideas: Raise tuition rates for in-state and out-of-state students
Attract more out-of-state or international students who pay full tuition
Expand high-demand graduate programs (e.g., MBA, Engineering) to grow grad enrollment
Offer online or hybrid programs to reach non-traditional students

categories.name: Revenue — Endowment & Donations
ideas: Launch an alumni engagement and annual giving campaign to grow the active donor base
Target major gift fundraising from top alumni
Name buildings or programs after large donors

categories.name: Revenue — Athletics & Other
ideas: Improve athletics revenue through ticket sales, sponsorships, and licensing
Explore corporate partnerships or executive education programs
Rent facilities (sports venues, conference rooms) to external parties

categories.name: Cost Reduction
ideas: Consolidate or eliminate under-enrolled academic programs
Reduce administrative overhead through shared services
Pursue energy efficiency and facilities optimization

categories.name: Grants — Expand Beyond Psychology
ideas: Hire grant-writing staff to increase application volume across departments
Leverage Economics department for research grants
Pursue federal STEM grants in Engineering

recommendation: Hamm's University should hire at least 22 additional faculty researchers — prioritizing the Psychology department given its existing prestige — to increase research grant revenue by $25M/year and return net income to +$20M within 2 years.
risks: New researchers may not achieve the same grant success rate (1.6 grants/researcher) as historical averages
The total addressable psychology grant market may not be large enough to absorb this much additional grant activity
Rapidly scaling research staff could create administrative strain or dilute brand/academic quality
Grants are typically awarded ~1 year after application, so benefits may lag beyond the 2-year target window
next_steps: Determine how many researchers Hamm's can physically accommodate given space constraints on campus
Conduct market research to quantify the total Psychology (and adjacent) grant market and estimate achievable share
Assemble a hiring team and begin identifying and interviewing researcher candidates
Explore complementary revenue levers (alumni giving, graduate program expansion) to reduce dependence on a single strategy
